new_conflicts_not_in_first_search.where: SSRN preprint of the CMAME NeuroSEM paper
new_conflicts_not_in_first_search.finding: DOI 10.2139/ssrn.4912094, title 'Neurosem: A Hybrid Framework ...', 2024, same six authors. The first search mentioned an SSRN version but gave no DOI. It is the top Crossref bibliographic hit for 'neurosem', so the conflict takes up the first two Crossref results.

Created 2026-07-11, pushed 2026-07-23. It registers 'neurosem' as a runtime model key in src/navier_cfd/runtime_registry.py and lists NeuroSEM in its model catalogue and hybrid-acceleration case study. The CMAME name is already being reused as a lowercase software identifier in third-party scientific code.

Created 2023-05-04, pushed 2024-12-04, no license. MATLAB functions named neurosem_plot and neurosem_data analyse neural activity at the onset of seizure symptoms (seizure semiology, OPSCEA data). This is an existing 'neurosem' identifier in neuroscience code, a sense unrelated to semantics.

1,140 code hits. They include the CMAME citation in publication lists (e.g. cyclotomicextension.github.io) and many prompt files using the joke condition 'Neurosemantical Inversitis' (e.g. friuns2/BlackFriday-GPTs-Prompts). The identifier is noisy on GitHub even though no repository owns the exact package name.
102 code hits, e.g. a C inline clamp helper DriftClamp in Hexlord/project-drift and a driftClamp parameter in TheFaucett/stock-game. These are generic identifier collisions, not a named project.

The full index has no perturbprint-like name, but it has perturb-prefixed projects: perturbate, perturbation-classifiers, perturbation-kernel, perturbationx, perturbator, perturbers, perturbguard, perturb-hd, perturbio, perturbmerge, PerturbNet, perturbopy, perturbresidual, perturb-tools, perturbvi. None is identical; the prefix is only mildly crowded.

neurosem_verdict_check: Confirmed: do not keep 'NeuroSem'. Registry names are free (PyPI, conda-forge, npm, RTD, CRAN, GitHub user/org, USPTO backend). The identical or near-identical name already belongs to a 2024 arXiv / SSRN / 2025 CMAME computational framework with public code that third-party CFD code now uses as a model key, to an active GPL-3.0 neuroscience-and-language-model repository with the identical spelling (vafaei-ar/NeuroSem, pushed 2026-09-13, in submission freeze), to a commercial NeuroSEM domain registered since 2013, and to an NLP-derived coaching movement. The one correction: the fetched neurosem.com page gives US East Coast, US West Coast and Europe contacts, not the cities New York and San Francisco. The OpenAlex SEM counts could not be re-checked.

alternatives_ranking_check.name: PerturbPrint
alternatives_ranking_check.note: Cleanest of the three: zero hits in every index that answered, including GitHub code search. Only a mild perturb- prefix crowd on PyPI and the Perturb-seq association noted earlier (that association was not re-verified because WebSearch was unavailable).

alternatives_ranking_check.name: DriftClamp
alternatives_ranking_check.note: Registries and literature clean, but 102 GitHub code hits for existing DriftClamp/driftClamp identifiers were missed earlier. Its semantic ambiguity with recording drift and clamp hardware is unchanged (not re-verified).

alternatives_ranking_check.name: EphysPrint
alternatives_ranking_check.note: No exact conflicts, but 47 PyPI projects contain 'ephys', and 'electrophysiological fingerprint' is established wording for recorded cells, so the name reads as a tool for experimental data rather than models.

final_recommendation: Agree with the first search: rename before Milestone 1 creates src/neurosem, the CLI or CITATION.cff. PerturbPrint (package and CLI 'perturbprint') is preferred. It was the only one of the three with zero hits in every source that answered in this re-check, GitHub code search included, and it maps onto the handoff's defined term 'perturbation fingerprint'. DriftClamp remains runner-up, slightly weaker than first reported because of existing code-identifier collisions. EphysPrint is third. This is not legal clearance: EUIPO, WIPO, company registries, Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, ACM DL, OpenAlex, Zenodo and (partly) Semantic Scholar were not successfully checked here. The final choice is Neel's, and PyPI, conda-forge, GitHub and USPTO should be re-checked immediately before M1.
